title: Lumbar percentage contribution to trunk (T12) range in flexion, extension and lateral flexion (no-LBP adults)

quantity.name: lumbar share of trunk ROM
quantity.definition: lumbar ROM / trunk (T12) ROM x 100 at peak, per subject then averaged. Trunk = T12 sensor angle; pelvis = S2 sensor angle; lumbar = trunk - pelvis (T12 relative to S2). Values = mean (between-subject SD) of the average of 3 test sessions.

source.authors: Laird RA, Kent P, Keating JL
source.n: 32 without LBP (42% F) [+30 chronic LBP, 50% F, reported in separate test]
source.sample: adults without LBP (NoLBP) recruited from physiotherapy clinics and a university; BMI<=30
source.age: NoLBP 35.5 (SD 12.4) y; LBP 45.8 (SD 11.6) y (groups differ, p=.001)

protocol.summary: Whole-range lumbo-pelvic rhythm expressed as % lumbar contribution (Table 3).
how_to_use: At full flexion assign 51.3% of T12 rotation to the lumbar spine and the rest to the pelvis (L/P ~ 1.05 from shares; ~0.95 from mean angles).
Lateral flexion: ~78-79% lumbar; extension: ~68% lumbar but SD 32%.
Use MDC90 (flexion 11.5%, extension 56.2%, lateral 10.4-11.8%) as robustness bands.

measurement.device: ViMove (DorsaVi) wireless IMUs on skin over T12 and S2 spinous processes, ~20 Hz
measurement.task: 5 repetitions each of max flexion, extension, left/right lateral flexion (reps 2-5 averaged); 3 test sessions (2 raters same day, 1 rater 7-14 d later)

protocol.notes: MDC90 (different-day, same rater) given per value as mdc90_days: use as the expected test-retest band for robustness runs. Total sample stated as n=63 in abstract but Table 1 lists 32 NoLBP + 30 LBP; Table 4 lists n per movement (NoLBP flexion 32, extension 31, lordosis/lateral 33).

extraction.check_notes: Re-read from layout text of Tables 2-3; left lateral flexion averages printed with negative sign (direction) - stored as magnitudes.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
